title: Quick check: Revalidation Strategies

questions.prompt: In the context of “Revalidation Strategies” and “Time-based revalidation”, Before caching data, what is the most important correctness question?
options: Whether private data can share one global cache key across users.
Whether the same defaults apply to every Next.js release.
Whether the data may be shared, how fresh it must be, and which user/request dimensions affect the result.
questions.answer_key: Whether the data may be shared, how fresh it must be, and which user/request dimensions affect the result.
questions.explanation: Cache behavior depends on the configured model and data sensitivity; user-specific results must not leak across cache boundaries.

questions.prompt: While implementing “Revalidation Strategies”, What should happen when a mutation changes content that was cached?
options: Assume all clients refresh automatically in every situation.
Invalidate or revalidate the relevant route/data according to the chosen cache strategy.
Disable authorization until the cache expires.
questions.answer_key: Invalidate or revalidate the relevant route/data according to the chosen cache strategy.
questions.explanation: A cache strategy needs an explicit path or tag invalidation plan that matches which data changed.

questions.prompt: When reviewing “Revalidation Strategies”, Which approach is safest for user-specific data?
options: Cache every response globally by URL only, regardless of identity.
Rely on hiding a result in CSS.
Treat a local development test as proof of all production behavior.
Use request/user-appropriate cache boundaries and verify that one user cannot receive another user’s response.
questions.answer_key: Use request/user-appropriate cache boundaries and verify that one user cannot receive another user’s response.
questions.explanation: Cache isolation is a security property and should be tested alongside freshness and performance.
